9: /// Use case: The managed IecBus state machine correctly implements the IEC
10: /// serial bus ATN-response and bit-clock protocol timing as specified by
11: /// the Commodore IEC serial bus standard.
13: /// ATN-response timing (Tat): A device must assert CLK low (and DATA low)
14: /// within Tat = 1ms of ATN going low. At the C64 PAL clock (985,248 Hz)
15: /// this is 985 cycles. The C64-side IecBus manager (the host) asserts CLK
16: /// simultaneously with ATN as part of the ATN send sequence, releasing CLK
17: /// to signal "ready to send" after all devices have responded. This test
18: /// validates that IecBus.Tick() transitions CLK and DATA to the correct
19: /// asserted (low = false) state within the spec window when ATN is set low.
21: /// VICE reference: iecbus.c:247-266 (ATN change -> VIA1 CA1 signal for 1541
22: /// ATN response), serial-iec-bus.c (IEC protocol state machine),
24: /// Commodore IEC spec: Tat (ATN turnaround) = 0-1000 microseconds.
28:     // Maximum cycles allowed for ATN response per IEC spec.

30:     // window (conservative; actual VICE ROM response is typically < 100 cycles).
